chapter: Town Hall, Vanguard and large works
title: Learning to write for harp
summary: Mingus never studied harp writing; a harpist on a poetry date showed him what not to write.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, the tenor player was really a jazz tenor player, (inaudible), too, more than most people. They had a harp, didn't they?
I don't -- geez, I don't remember.
They said (inaudible) said it was a harp.
Did you like writing for harp? Did you go get an orchestration book and find out how to write for harp before you sat down and --
How did you do it, did you just write some glistens or --
No, it was like a harp with a bass part. It was just like a bass line.
Yeah, harp was the hardest damn thing for me to learn about. And I went out and bought a book and broke my neck trying to learn how to write for harp.

I learned that on a poetry date I did for a large mixed string group. I wrote the harp part and she said, 'Let me show you what not to write for harp.' And practically everything I'd written was incorrect.
You (inaudible) wrote a lot of chromatic stuff and everything, probably.
(Inaudible) do you know any chord changes, chord arpeggios. (Inaudible) She asked, 'Those are chord arpeggios. Start with that note, those are arpeggios.'
